name: Adam Howard
fact: He ran unopposed for vice president of administration in the April 2000 election, and was already SGA information technology director. The Herald described him as a Florence junior and a corporate and organizational communication major who had been in SGA for two years, and quoted him saying the office was one where he could put the majority of his strength to work for the student body.

name: Leslie McClard
fact: She ran unopposed for vice president of public relations in the April 2000 election, having joined SGA in her sophomore year at the urging of Cassie Martin. The Herald described her as a Scottsville junior and a public relations major, and named her the SGA committee head for the Senior Awards Banquet.

name: Darlene Lodmell
fact: She was elected SGA secretary in April 1996, beating Louisville sophomore David Apple by 313 votes to 293 in the closest race on the ballot. The Herald called her a Versailles sophomore and quoted her thanking Apple, saying he ran a really good campaign and she was sure SGA could use him somewhere. She was sworn in at the SGA banquet later that month, and the paper identified her as the twin sister of Carlene Lodmell, who took office the same night as vice president.

name: Steve Roadcap
fact: He ran unopposed for SGA treasurer in the April 1996 election and was sworn in at the SGA banquet, where the Herald described him as a Louisville sophomore. Earlier that month, asked whether student government was too Greek, he told the paper that Greeks are asked to join SGA and that there are more Greeks than independents because they are encouraged to get involved.

name: Shawna Whartenby
fact: She ran unopposed for SGA public relations director in April 1996 and was sworn in at the SGA banquet as a Louisville sophomore. At the same banquet she received the Outstanding Congress Member Award.

name: Anne Guillory
fact: The Herald quoted her as a Bowling Green junior in April 1996, discussing a lecture on Robert E. Lee by the historian Emory M. Thomas, and the university's honours list printed in the same month gives her full name as Anne Katherine Guillory. In April 1996 she also wrote to the paper urging students not to complain if they did not vote.

name: Jamie Fite
fact: She won the SGA secretary's race in April 1997, beating the sitting secretary Darlene Lodmell by 452 votes to 396. The Herald described her as a sophomore from Hermitage, Tennessee, and reported that the secretary primary was cancelled for the first time in recent memory once a third candidate, Matt Bastin, was disqualified for not having thirty earned credit hours.

name: Steve Roadcap
fact: He stood for re-election as SGA treasurer in April 1997 and lost to Chad Lewis, a sophomore from Scottsburg, Indiana, by 518 votes to 327. The Herald called him the current treasurer and a Louisville junior.

name: Darlene Lodmell
fact: She stood for a second term as SGA secretary in April 1997 and lost to Jamie Fite by 452 votes to 396. The Herald called her a Versailles junior and the sitting secretary.

name: Anne Guillory
fact: She sat in on the Board of Regents meeting of spring 1996 that raised student fees by twenty-five dollars to pay for gender equity in sports, and the Herald photographed her reaction to the roll call. She told the paper the most depressing thing she found was that the student regent voted for the fee. The caption calls her a Bowling Green junior.

name: Shawna Whartenby
fact: In April 1996 she campaigned for the package of constitutional amendments on the SGA ballot, writing to the Herald to urge a yes vote, and the paper quoted her as an SGA member arguing that students should have a high grade point average to hold office. She was a Louisville sophomore.

name: Anne Guillory
fact: As chairwoman of the legislative research committee she led the rewriting of the SGA constitution that Congress adopted in March 1998. The Herald quoted her, a Bowling Green senior, saying the old document was disorganised and contradicted itself, and that what the committee wanted was a unified, cohesive, easy-to-read constitution. The new version gave the president full veto power over legislation, subject to a written explanation within forty-eight hours.

name: Kip Carr
fact: The Herald printed an editor's note with his letter of 23 April 1998 identifying him as chairman of the SGA technology committee in 1996-97 and chairman of the bylaws recision subcommittee in 1997. Writing from Atlanta as a former student, he argued against the proposed replacement of the SGA bylaws before the vote the following Tuesday, saying the open and accessible principle in the existing bylaws was not a bad idea.

name: Tim Gilbert
fact: When SGA membership fell from 81 to 65 in the autumn of 1998 and long debates were blamed, he defended the legislative research committee he sat on. The Herald quoted him saying some members do not realise how thoroughly bills and resolutions are reviewed before they reach the floor, and that people who joined the committee would get their say on all the bills. He also allowed that some votes may be influenced by familiarity or friendship with the author rather than by the legislation.

name: Jeff Baynham
fact: He helped rebuild the SGA web page over the summer of 1998, working with public relations director Brad Sweatt on the version unveiled in the first week of the autumn semester. The Herald called him a Lexington sophomore and quoted him saying the site was looking really good and that students would be curious and click in to see what SGA could offer them. He wanted an SGA link on the front of the university's own site.

name: Jason Chilton
fact: He wrote the bill, passed by SGA in December 1998, that set up a new member orientation seminar in the first month of each semester to teach new members the structure and purpose of SGA and parliamentary procedure. The Herald quoted him at the meeting saying it was geared to getting new members involved and making meetings run more smoothly.

name: Mitchell Bailey
fact: He argued that SGA should have taken part in the disaster relief after a fire at the Kappa Alpha Order house in the autumn of 1998, when Congress voted the fraternity's aid bill down. The Herald quoted him saying it was the role of a government to offer support to those it represents.

name: Amy Risley
fact: She graduated in May 1998, at the end of her year in SGA Congress. The journalism department's advertisement congratulating its May graduates lists her under public relations.

name: Jamie Fite
fact: She entered SGA in the autumn of 1996 as a new coed representative and sat on the task force that reviewed dormitory rules and the Hilltopics student guide, telling the Herald that serving on it would benefit students. In October 1996 she helped write the resolution asking the university to put a large screen television with closed captioning in Garrett Center, and the paper ran her words as a pull quote: the one they have now does not work very well, and it is a very frequently used place. The Herald called her a Nashville junior.

name: Ryan Faught
fact: He was chosen as a WKU Spirit Master, one of the university's student ambassadors, in September 1997, and was still serving as a returning member a year later. The Herald called him a Bowling Green junior when the new intake was announced.

name: Jamie Fite
fact: As SGA secretary she went with the rest of the executive to a student leadership conference in Savannah, Georgia in the summer of 1997, alongside treasurer Chad Lewis and public relations director Heather Rogers. The Herald described her as a senior from Hermitage, Tennessee.

name: Darlene Lodmell
fact: After her year as SGA secretary she became executive chairwoman of the University Center Board. The Herald quoted her, as a Versailles senior, describing the board's committees for concerts, special events and lectures and its work on Big Red's Roar.

name: Shawna Whartenby
fact: As SGA public relations director she ran the organisation's autumn 1996 publicity: a pep rally on the Downing University Center south lawn with munch money for the sorority that turned out the most people, and an open meet-and-greet meeting so students could meet their representatives and the executive officers. The Herald called her a Louisville junior and quoted her saying students had not felt they could talk to SGA.

name: Adam Howard
fact: He sat on the legislative research committee in the autumn of 1998 and spoke against the resolution asking the city for telephones outside the dormitories, telling Congress that its authors had not contacted the city and had not researched it enough.

name: Anne Guillory
fact: She spoke in the November 1997 debate on housing scholarships, which SGA Congress voted 35 to 15 to ask the university to make payable off campus. The Herald quoted her saying she felt tied to living in the dormitories because she did not want to live at home and did not have the money for an apartment.

name: David Wilkins
fact: A Bardstown freshman and a member of SGA, he was the organisation's sharpest internal critic in 1998-99. He wrote to the Herald in November 1998 accusing SGA of being self-serving and of ignoring debate, and again a week later that it punished free speech, and when the paper looked back on the semester in January 1999 he told it that any bad publicity SGA got was its own fault, because things were passed and decisions made that made the organisation look foolish. The paper ran that line as a pull quote.

name: Jason Chilton
fact: He defended SGA against its critics in January 1999, telling the Herald that some of the publicity the organisation had received was undeserved and very negative. The paper called him a Lawrenceburg junior.

name: Steve Roadcap
fact: As chairman of SGA's campus improvements committee he organised the campus clean-up of 18 October 1995, telling the Herald it was a good thing to do after Homecoming because of the litter, and took two proposals to Congress the following week, to pave the Creason lot behind Egypt and to put a rail beside Schneider Hall. The committee heads voted him SGA member of the month for September 1995. The Herald called him a Louisville sophomore.

name: Shawna Whartenby
fact: She spoke for the committee heads who voted Steve Roadcap SGA member of the month in September 1995, telling the Herald that from the very beginning he had been really active putting together legislation and was doing an outstanding job. The paper called her a Louisville sophomore.

name: Darlene Lodmell
fact: She chaired SGA's student affairs committee in 1995-96 and argued for security cameras on campus, telling the Herald in November 1995 that they would promote security for students, especially women. Earlier that autumn, as a Versailles sophomore, she had been elected to represent the College of Educational and Behavioral Sciences.

name: Todd Osterloh
fact: He ran Western's men's volleyball club. The Herald's campus life column of 31 August 1999 gave him as the contact for the club's organisational meeting and open gym at the Preston Center, and said the team would practise twice a week and compete in open and collegiate tournaments through the year.

name: David Wilkins
fact: He competed for Western's forensics team. The Herald reported him placing in extemporaneous and impromptu speaking at a tournament at Tennessee State University in the autumn of 1999, and called him a Bardstown sophomore, a year on from the Bardstown freshman it had quoted as an SGA member.
